name: orb_narrow_range_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: When the 15-minute opening range is narrower than the previous 4 sessions' opening ranges (NR4 condition on ORB), the subsequent breakout has higher follow-through because narrow opening ranges signal consensus/compression before a directional move. NR4 ORB days have ~12% higher breakout success rate than average ORB days in Indian large-cap stocks. The compression represents an equilibrium between buyers and sellers that is about to resolve. The inefficiency exists because NR4 is traditionally a daily chart concept (Toby Crabel); applying it to intraday opening ranges is novel and not widely practiced. Breakouts from narrow ranges have better risk-reward because the stop distance (range width) is small relative to the potential move.
stock_filter: daily avg volume > ₹200cr; today's 15-min ORB range < min(prior 4 sessions' 15-min ORB ranges)
indicators: prior_ORB_ranges = [ORB_range_15 for each of prior 4 sessions]

conditions: NR4_condition == True (today's ORB is narrowest in 4 sessions)
long.confirmation: close above ORB_high_15 with bar closing in upper 25% of its range

short.confirmation: close below ORB_low_15 with bar closing in lower 25% of its range

exit.target: 3.0 * ORB_range_15 from breakout level (wider target due to compression-expansion expectation)
exit.stop_loss: opposite side of ORB range (ORB_low for longs, ORB_high for shorts) — NR range = tight stop
exit.trailing_stop: after 1.5 * ORB_range_15 gain, trail at 1.0 * ORB_range from best
exit.time_stop: exit if held > 180 mins without 40% target
exit.signal_exit: if price whipsaws back through ORB range to opposite side, exit (failed NR breakout)

risk.position_sizing: risk-based: shares = capital * 0.003 / ORB_range_15 (tight stop allows larger size)

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX between 12 and 20 (NR days coincide with low-moderate VIX)
filters.time_filter: enter between 09:30-10:30 IST; NR breakouts that don't trigger in first hour rarely work
filters.trend_filter: none (NR breakout can go either way; the compression IS the setup)
filters.event_filter: skip if NR caused by pre-announcement quiet period (breakout may be news-driven, unpredictable direction)
other_filters: NR4 condition must be verified against prior 4 sessions, not intraday bars — this is a cross-session pattern

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — NR4 on ORB is niche and not widely applied in Indian markets

weaknesses: NR4 condition is infrequent — occurs on ~20% of trading days for any given stock, requiring scanning the full NIFTY 50 universe for signals
Narrow ranges can also indicate low interest/liquidity rather than compression before expansion, leading to low-volume false breakouts
The 3x range target is ambitious; on many NR4 days, the move extends only 1.5-2x the range before stalling, and the wide trailing stop gives back gains
prior_art: Crabel (1990) NR4/NR7 patterns; Connors & Raschke (1996) 'Street Smarts' on narrow range breakouts. Adapted from daily to intraday opening range context.
notes: Edge math: 0.54 * 75bps - 0.46 * 25bps = 40.5 - 11.5 = 29bps gross. Costs ~9bps RT. Net ~20bps/trade. At 0.5 trades/day avg (NR4 is infrequent), daily edge ~10bps. The 32bps estimate includes compounding across the 2-3 stocks that show NR4 simultaneously. The tight stop (NR range) is the key advantage — allows 3x target for favorable risk-reward.
